svg.aria-label: A layered dependency graph of the To-Do-List build. Eight horizontal lanes are the eight epics, grouped into three tiers: Tier 1 is Epics 1 to 5, Tier 2 is Epics 6 and 7, Tier 3 is Epic 8. Thirty-eight story boxes sit in eleven columns; a column is the earliest wave in which a story can be built, so stories in the same column have no dependency on each other. Fifty-three arrows are prerequisites pointing from the story that must ship first to the story that waits for it. Curved arrows stay inside one epic; straight coloured rails cross between epics and are coloured by the epic they leave. Epic 1 starts alone in column 0 with Story 1.1, the clean clone and first-run surface. Epic 2 starts at column 3 with Story 2.1, the Rule Engine. Epic 3 starts at column 3 with Story 3.1, the derived lists. Story 4.1, the committed Fixture, is the FR-19 gate: Stories 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 7.1 and 7.2 all depend on it. Epic 5 runs from column 6 to column 9 and ends the Tier 1 deliverable. Epic 6 runs from column 5 to column 10 and depends only on Story 2.6. Epic 7 runs from column 8 to column 10 and needs both the harness and the Model Engine adapter. Epic 8, the three cuttable refinements, depends on Epics 2 and 3 and nothing depends on it.
svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: To-Do-List — 8 epics, 38 stories, and the order they must be built in
Every arrow is a prerequisite: the story an arrow points to cannot start until the story it leaves has shipped. Lanes are epics, read top to bottom; the build runs left to right.
A column is the earliest wave a story can be built in — two stories in the same column have no dependency between them, so either order works. Generated from .docs/planning-artifacts/epics.md.

Cutting is deleting whole epics from the bottom, never stories from the middle (PRD section 6.3 cut order, AD-10): drop Epic 8, then Epic 7, then Epic 6, and every remaining arrow still has its source.
prerequisite across epics, coloured by the epic it leaves
Story 4.1 is the FR-19 gate: 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 7.1 and 7.2 all wait for it
story box: id, what it delivers, and its lead requirement

53 prerequisite edges, all pointing forwards: no story in this figure depends on a story to its right, inside its epic or outside it. Story titles are shortened to fit — epics.md carries the full title, the acceptance criteria and the spine row for each one.
Waves are a dependency fact, not a schedule: one builder works one story at a time, and bmad-sprint-planning flattens this graph into the single ordered queue in sprint-status.md.
Illustrative figure for IBE160 · To-Do-List · drawn 2026-11-22 from the approved epic breakdown. Where this figure and epics.md disagree, epics.md governs.
